mainEntity.name: How do you calculate cost per hire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add internal recruitment costs (recruiter time, tools, interview hours) and external costs (ads, agencies, assessments) for a defined period, then divide by the number of hires completed in that same period. The EarlyJobs calculator applies this standard formula using amounts you enter in INR.

Include the portion of recruiter or HR compensation attributable to hiring activity if your finance team tracks it that way. Some organisations allocate by headcount or percentage of role — pick one method and use it consistently when comparing quarters or plants.

mainEntity.name: Does cost per hire include employee salaries?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Cost per hire covers spending to fill a role, not the employee's post-joining wages, statutory contributions, or bonuses. Keep recruitment spend separate so you can compare channels and agencies without mixing payroll.

mainEntity.name: What if there are zero hires?

acceptedAnswer.text: You cannot calculate a meaningful average cost per hire when no one joined in the period — the tool avoids dividing by zero and prompts you to adjust dates or hire counts. Recruitment spend still matters for reporting; pair it with funnel metrics instead.
